transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I came in 'cause... I just feel like I got this motor running inside me all day long. Kinda like my buddy Dale's old Chevy truck, you know? The one that always idled way too high. He tried fixing the carburetor on that thing a few years back, and we spent a whole weekend in his garage just messing with it. He ended up moving down to Florida, though, so I don't see him much anymore. 

But yeah, wait, what was I saying? Right, the motor thing. It's just... if I have to sit still, like at church, or even out there in your waiting room—which, by the way, the magazines out there are really old, I was flipping through one about fishing from like three years ago—or even just sitting around at home, I feel completely trapped. I just gotta get up or do something, you know? I can't just sit.
Do you find yourself feeling restless or unable to sit still, even when you want to?

Yeah, exactly! That's exactly what I meant just now about the motor and feeling trapped. It don't matter if I actually *want* to just sit there. 

Like, if I try to just sit on the couch and watch a movie... oh, my brother actually gave me his password for the movie channels on the TV. He drives one of those bucket trucks for the cable company now. He always says he's gonna talk to his boss and get me a job doing it, but man, I don't know about the heights. I got up on my roof last year to clean out the gutters and got so spooked I almost couldn't get back over to the ladder. Took me like forty-five minutes just to climb down. 

But yeah, even if it's a really good movie and I want to watch it, I just can't stay put. My legs start going, and I get that trapped feeling all over again, and I just gotta get up and pace around the living room or find something to mess with. I just can't stay in the chair.
Have you noticed that you feel tired or lack energy most days, even when you haven't been doing much?

Nah, not really. I don't ever feel tired like that. Honestly, it's the opposite, I'm pretty much always wired. 

My buddy Earl, though, he's tired all the time. He works the graveyard shift down at that gas station on Route 9. They just put in one of those new slushie machines in there, the blue raspberry kind? Man, I love those things. I walked all the way down there at like three in the morning the other day 'cause I was just wide awake and couldn't stop pacing around my kitchen, so I figured I might as well go get a drink and stretch my legs. Earl was practically snoring behind the register when I walked in. He's got this old basset hound that sleeps under the counter with him, too. Cutest dog, but man, it smells terrible, kind of like wet corn chips. 

But uh... wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, being tired. Yeah, no, I don't really get tired. I just keep going.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about things, even when there's no clear reason to worry?

Worrying? No, not really. I don't sit around chewing my nails over stuff, you know? I mean, unless I actually got something to worry about. 

Like when my cousin Jimmy borrowed my lawnmower. I was pretty worried about that, 'cause Jimmy's got this habit of breaking things. He borrowed my weed whacker last summer and somehow melted the plastic guard clean off. I still don't even know how he did it, he said he was just edging the driveway, but I swear he must've held it over a fire or something. He's always getting into weird stuff like that. Last I heard, he bought a metal detector and is trying to find pirate treasure out by the lake. I told him the only thing he's gonna find out there is old beer cans and maybe some rusty fish hooks. My uncle caught a massive catfish out there once, though. Thing was huge, practically the size of a dog. We had a big fish fry and everything. 

But yeah, anyway... I don't really worry about stuff just out of nowhere. I'm usually moving too fast to sit and think about things going wrong anyway.
Do you often find yourself moving, fidgeting, or pacing even when you're in situations where you're supposed to stay still, like in meetings, at work, or during meals?

Yeah, all the time. It's like my body just won't let me stay in the chair. Like if I'm in a waiting room, or eating dinner, or... well, I don't go to meetings really, but anytime I'm supposed to just sit there, I end up popping up. I'll get up to get a drink of water, or I'll go look out the window to see what's happening outside. 

I actually saw the craziest thing out the window at the DMV last month. I was waiting to get my ID renewed, which is a whole story 'cause they lost my paperwork three times. But anyway, I'm looking out the window and this guy in a pickup truck tries to parallel park, right? And he just backs straight up onto the hood of a Honda Civic. Just right up on it! The lady in the Civic comes flying out of the DMV yelling her head off, and the guy in the truck is just sitting there looking confused. Turns out he had his dog in the front seat and the dog jumped on his lap or something. It was a pitbull mix, looked a lot like my neighbor's dog, Buster. Buster got out last week and chased the mailman down the block. I felt bad for the mailman, he's a nice guy, always gives me those coupons for the pizza place down the street. 

But uh, yeah, I do that a lot. I'll just be standing up and moving around, and then I realize everybody else is still sitting down and just staring at me. It's kinda embarrassing, but I just can't help it.
Do you often find yourself interrupting others or acting without thinking, like blurting out answers before someone finishes asking a question?

Yeah, man, I do that all the time. It's like the words just shoot right out of my mouth before my brain even catches up. I'll jump in with an answer before someone is even done talking. Like, the pastor at church, or my cousin, or the lady down at the food pantry... I'll just blurt something out, and then halfway through I realize I answered the completely wrong thing or, you know, I just made 'em mad because I cut 'em off. 

The pantry lady, she gets real huffy about it. Her name's Brenda. She wears these giant glasses with the little rhinestones on the corners, you know the ones? My grandma used to have glasses exactly like that. Grandma used to make this peach cobbler that would just melt in your mouth. We'd go over there every Sunday after church, and she'd have it baking in the oven. You could smell it from the driveway. She had this huge oak tree in the front yard where we used to build forts. We found a whole nest of baby raccoons up in there once. Cutest little things, but man, their mom was mean. Chased my brother all the way to the porch. He tripped over the garden hose and scraped his knee so bad he had to get stitches. 

But yeah... what was I saying? Oh, right, blurting stuff out. Yeah, I do that a lot. I just can't seem to wait my turn to speak.
Do you find it hard to focus or stay concentrated on tasks, like following instructions, staying organized, or finishing what you start?

Yeah, I definitely have a hard time with that. Like, if someone is trying to explain something to me, I'll be right there with 'em at first. But then... I don't know, my brain just kinda drifts off. Like when my buddy is trying to figure out ride times to get me to the food pantry, or Brenda is running through the pantry list, or even at church when they're going over the plans for the week. I listen good for the first minute, and then I'm just gone. Next thing I know, they're looking at me waiting for an answer, and I missed the whole middle part that I actually needed to hear. 

It happened last week with the ride times. My buddy, Dave, he drives this old Ford Ranger. The thing is held together with duct tape and rust, I swear. He bought it off this guy who used to race dirt bikes out by the quarry. You ever been out to the quarry? It's real deep, filled with this bright blue water. Some kids jump off the cliffs there, which is crazy dangerous. One kid broke his leg doing it a couple years back, had to get airlifted out and everything. Cost his parents a fortune. They had to sell their boat to pay for it. It was a nice boat, too, one of those pontoon ones with the little grill on the back. We used to go out on a boat like that when I was a kid. My dad would grill hot dogs... 

But anyway, yeah. I start off listening, but then I just lose track of what people are saying, and I miss the important stuff. It's frustrating, you know?
When did you first start noticing these symptoms? Were they something you experienced even as a kid, or did they come on more recently?

Oh, man, it's been like this forever. Like, way back. Even when I was a little boy in school, it was the same deal. The teachers were always getting on me, always moving my seat to the front or the back or next to their desk because I just could not stay put. I was always talking out of turn, getting in trouble for jumping up and trying to leave before the bell even rang or the class was done. 

I remember Mrs. Higgins in the third grade, she had this big ruler she'd smack on the chalkboard. She'd smack that thing so hard I thought it was gonna break in half. She drove this old yellow Volkswagen Beetle. We used to try and punch each other when we saw it pull into the parking lot. "Punch buggy yellow," you know? My brother got me so good on the arm once, left a bruise for like two weeks. He was always doing stuff like that. He got this boxing set for Christmas one year, the kind with the big inflatable gloves. We'd go out in the snow and just wail on each other. My mom would get so mad 'cause we'd come in all wet and track snow all over her nice rug. She bought that rug at a flea market... or maybe it was a yard sale? There used to be this huge yard sale every summer over by the fairgrounds. They had the best funnel cakes at the fairgrounds.

But yeah, anyway, the teachers were always on my case about not sitting still and blurting stuff out. So it's definitely not a new thing, it's been my whole life, really.
